questions.question: Which of the following was a Ceylonese chronicle that acted as an important literary source of the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
Mahavamsa
It was written by Mahanama in Pali language.
Literary Sources of Mauryan Period:
  • "Arthashastra" (Kautilya)
  • "Indica" (Megasthenes)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Chandragupta Maurya:
(a) Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan Empire.
(b) He fasted to death at Shravanabelagola following Jainism.
(c) His Greek name was Megasthenes, and he captured Pataliputra in 322 BCE by defeating Dhanananda of the Sarnath dynasty.
Which of the above statements is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
C only
Chandragupta Maurya's Greek name was Sandrocottos, not Megasthenes. Megasthenes was the Greek historian who visited Chandragupta's court.

questions.question: What was the function of an officer called Samaharta?
questions.solution:
Tax assessment
Officers during the Mauryan administration:
  • Shulkadhyaksha - Officer-in-charge of royal income
  • Koshadhyaksha - Treasury officer
  • Lakshanadhyaksha - Coin minting
  • Rajjukas - Land measurer
  • Yukta - Subordinate revenue officer
  • Sannidata - Treasury head
  • Panyadhyaksha - Office of commerce department
  • Samaharta - Tax assessment/Collector General of Revenue

questions.question: Emperor Ashoka conquered Kalinga after how many years of his coronation?
questions.solution:
8 years
Ashoka fought the Kalinga War in 261 BC. King Ashoka (268 - 232 BC) was the third king of the Mauryan Empire.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Mauryan provincial administration:
A. The Mauryan Empire was divided into Janapadas (provinces), each headed by a Mahamatra.
B. Each province had a Kumar or Kumara appointed as provincial governor.
C. The Rajjukas were officials in charge of agriculture and land revenue collection.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A and C only
No position called Kumar/Kumara existed as governor; provinces were administered by Mahamatra.

questions.question: How many classes of Indian society are mentioned in Megasthenes book Indica?
questions.solution:
7
They were: Brahmin (upper class), Philosophers, Farmers, Herders, Artisans, Military, Overseers, Councillors and Assessors.

questions.question: According to Kautilya's Arthashastra, the Commanding Officer of the cavalry in the Mauryan administration was known as:
questions.solution:
Ashwadhyaksha
Officers in Mauryan Empire:
  • Mantrin - Chief Minister
  • Senapati - Commander-in-Chief
  • Yuvraj - Crown prince
  • Shulkadhyaksha - Officer in-charge of royal income
  • Prashasti - Prison head
  • Koshadhyaksha - Treasury officer
  • Vyabharika - Chief Judge
  • Dandapala - Head of Police
  • Annapala - Head of food grains department
  • Pradeshika - District administrator
  • Hastyadhyaksha - Chief Commander of Elephant Corps
  • Rathadhyaksha - Chief Commander of Chariot Corps
  • Nayaka - City security officer
  • Ashwadhyaksha - Commanding Officer of the cavalry

questions.question: The Mauryan pillar capital found at ______ is popularly known as the Lion Capital.
questions.solution:
Sarnath
Lion Capital - Erected by Ashoka (Around 250 BCE) in commemoration of Dhammachakra pravartana or the first sermon of Buddha. The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath is the Indian National Emblem.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Arthashastra is the manual of Mauryan administration and military organisation.
Reason (R): It was authored by Varahamihira in Sanskrit.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, R is true
questions.solution:
A is true, R is false
Arthashastra was authored by Kautilya (Chanakya/Vishnugupta), not Varahamihira. Varahamihira authored Brihat Samitha, which deals with astrology, architecture, and planetary calculations.

questions.question: Nagarjuni Caves were donated to which of the following sects by Mauryans?
questions.solution:
Ajivika
It was founded by Goshala Maskariputra. It is based on the philosophy that the affairs of the entire universe were ordered by a cosmic force called Niyati that determined all events, including an individual's fate. The seven caves were created by Mauryan time for the Ajivika Sect.

questions.question: As per the contents mentioned in Ashokan inscriptions, how many major political centres were there in the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
Five
The five major political centres of the Mauryan empire were located at Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Mauryan Empire maintained a state monopoly over mining and trade.
Reason (R): Kautilya's Arthashastra prescribes state control over mines, forests, salt, and trade to increase revenue.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, R is true
questions.solution:
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
The Mauryan state directly controlled resources and trade, as prescribed in Arthashastra, to ensure revenue and economic stability.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was called Amitrochates by the Greeks?
questions.solution:
Bindusara
He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and was the second Mauryan emperor of India whose reign from 297 - 273 BCE.

questions.question: There were several cities in the Mauryan empire. Which of the following cities was located on the southernmost side?
questions.solution:
Brahmagiri
The Maurya Empire:
  • Founder - Chandragupta Maurya
  • Capital - Pataliputra (modern Patna)
  • Three important rulers - Chandragupta, his son Bindusara, and Bindusara's son Ashoka

questions.question: Which of the following places does not contain the major inscription of Ashoka?
questions.solution:
Sanchi
It is a famous Buddhist site with several stupas and monasteries. Language used in Ashoka's inscriptions - Prakrit. Ashoka's name is only used in four locations: Maski, Brahmagiri (Karnataka), Gujara (Madhya Pradesh) and Nettur (Andhra Pradesh).

questions.question:
Identify the correct statements regarding the Pillars of Ashoka:
A. The Pillars of Ashoka were primarily built to spread the policies of Dharma.
B. All Pillars of Ashoka were erected during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya.
C. The Seventh Pillar Edict mentions Dhamma Mahamattas and is the longest among all pillar edicts.
questions.solution:
A and C only
Pillars were erected during Ashoka's reign, not Chandragupta Maurya's.

questions.question: Which caves are considered as the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India dating back to the Maurya period?
questions.solution:
Barabar and Nagarjuni caves
Located in Jehanabad district of Bihar, constructed by Emperor Ashoka for the benefit of Ajivika ascetics. They were cut from a single solid granite block.

questions.question: Somewhat before the time of the Mauryan empire, about ______ years ago, emperors in China began building the Great Wall.
questions.solution:
2400
Emperor Qin Shi Huang ordered construction of the Great Wall around 221 B.C. It was meant to protect the northern frontier of the empire from pastoral people.

questions.question: Pushyamitra, who was the commander of Brihadratha, the last Mauryan emperor, killed the king and established a new dynasty. Which of the following was his dynasty?
questions.solution:
Shunga Dynasty
  • Founder - Pushyamitra Sunga
  • Ruled - From 185 BCE to 73 BCE
  • Last Ruler - Devabhuti
  • Kanva Dynasty Founder - Vasudeva Kanva (73 BCE to 28 BCE), Last Ruler - Susarma
  • Satavahana Dynasty Founder - Simuka, Famous Ruler - Gautamiputra Satakarni

questions.question: Ashoka appointed ______ to solve the social problems in his region.
questions.solution:
Dhamma Mahamatta
Tirthas: The highest category of officials in the administration. There were 18 Tirthas.
  • Amatyas - High ranking officials almost like present-day secretaries
  • Sannidhata - Chief treasury
  • Samaharta - collector general of revenue
  • Yuktas - Subordinate officers responsible for the Empire's revenue
  • Rajjukas - Officers in charge of land measurement and boundary-fixing

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct?
I. Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were written in Brahmi script.
II. Many of Chanakya's ideas were written down in a book called the Arthashastra.
questions.solution:
Both I and II
Brahmi Script was deciphered by James Prinsep.

questions.question: Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts are found in different parts of India. Which of the following is NOT a find spot of Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
Rupnath
Minor rock edicts of Ashoka locations include: Kandahar (Afghanistan), Lampaka (Afghanistan), Bahapur (Delhi), Bariat (Rajasthan), Bhabru (Rajasthan), Gujarra (Madhya Pradesh), Rupnath (Madhya Pradesh), Panguraria (Madhya Pradesh), Sasaram (Bihar), Barabar Caves (Bihar), Rajula-Mandagiri (Andhra Pradesh), Suvarna Giri (Andhra Pradesh), Brahmagiri (Karnataka), JatinaRameshwara (Karnataka), Siddapur (Karnataka), Maski (Karnataka), Nittur (Karnataka), Udegolam (Karnataka), Palikgundu and Gayimath (Karnataka).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Kantakasodhana' court:
1. Kantakasodhana literally means 'removal of thorns.'
2. It was a type of civil court prevalent in the Mauryan Empire.
3. Kautilya's Arthashastra mentions cases that are subject to Kantakasodhana.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 and 3 only
Kantakasodhana was not a civil court, but a criminal court in the Mauryan Empire dealing with serious offenses.

questions.question: Who among the following published a set of Ashokan inscriptions in 1877?
questions.solution:
Alexander Cunningham
He was the founder of the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
A. Rudrasena II belonged to the Gupta dynasty.
B. He married Prabhvatigupta, daughter of Samudragupta.
C. Chandragupta II was the founder of the Vakataka dynasty.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
None of the above
  • Rudrasena II belonged to the Vakataka dynasty, not the Gupta dynasty
  • He married Prabhvatigupta, daughter of Chandragupta II, not Samudragupta
  • Chandragupta II was a Gupta ruler, not founder of the Vakataka dynasty (which was founded by Vindhyashakti)

questions.question: The ______ were tributary chiefs of the Gupta dynasty. They established an independent kingdom in western India. Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of this kingdom.
questions.solution:
Maitrakas
They established Valabhi as their capital and ruled until the middle of the eighth century. Dhruvasena II was a contemporary of Harshavardhana and was married to his daughter. Hsuan Tsang tells us that Dhruvasena II attended Harsha's assembly at Prayaga (Allahabad). Maukharies ruled over Kannauj, a city in western Uttar Pradesh; they were also subordinate rulers of the Guptas and used the title of samanta.

questions.question: Who among the following was the author of 'Brihat Katha Kosh'?
questions.solution:
Harisena
He was a Sanskrit writer and poet in the court of Samudragupta. "Brihat Katha Kosh" is a collection of ancient Indian folk tales and legends. Bhavabhuti is believed to be the court poet of King Yashovarman of Kannauj. His famous plays are Mahaviracharita and Malatimadhava.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Kalidasa:
I. Kalidasa was a famous poet and playwright in ancient India.
II. He was patronized by Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) of the Gupta Empire.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Both I and II
Kalidasa was one of the nine gems (Navaratnas) in the court of Chandragupta II. His famous works include Abhijnanasakuntalam, Meghadutam, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhavam, Malavikagnimitram, and Vikramorvashiyam.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Gupta dynasty is correct?
questions.option_1: The founder of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta I.
questions.option_2: The Gupta period is known as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India.
questions.option_3: The Gupta rulers were followers of Jainism.
questions.option_4: The Gupta Empire declined immediately after Samudragupta.
questions.solution:
The Gupta period is known as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India
  • The founder of the Gupta dynasty was Sri Gupta, not Chandragupta I
  • Gupta rulers were generally Hindus but tolerant of other religions
  • The Gupta Empire continued to flourish after Samudragupta under Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I, and Skandagupta
  • The Gupta period saw remarkable achievements in science, mathematics, astronomy, literature, and art

questions.question: Harisena, the author of Prayag Prashasti, was the court poet of which of the following Gupta emperors?
Gupta emperor Chandragupta I was the first ruler to adopt which of the following titles?
The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim Fa Hien visited India during the reign of which of the following Gupta emperors?
